evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.65: sphaerae figūra et cylindrī
Verg. G. 1.178: ārea cum prīmīs ingentī aequanda cylindrō, a roller for levelling the threshing floor
terms.comment: Greek κύλινδρος, with a short y. Cicero names it among the solid figures; it is also a stone roller for levelling the ground, which is what the shape is for (see “rolling pin”).

phrases.english: Roll up the paper: it makes a cylinder.

phrases.latin: Haec turris cylindrus est: rotunda et alta.
phrases.english: This tower is a cylinder: round and tall.

phrases.latin: At mihi vel cylindrī vel quadrātī vel cōnī vel pȳramidis vidētur esse fōrmōsior.
phrases.english: But to me the shape of a cylinder, or a cube, or a cone, or a pyramid seems more beautiful.

sources: Lewis & Short: cylindrus · Lewis & Short: cylindratus
